messages.text: Carrick: 'Not impossible' Man Utd can achieve Ferguson success again

metadata.summary: Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can reach the heights achieved under Sir Alex Ferguson but is not expecting the same level of patience.
metadata.content: Michael Carrick: Manchester United boss says it is possible club can emulate Sir Alex Ferguson's success at Old Trafford | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Michael Carrick: Manchester United boss says it is possible club can emulate Sir Alex Ferguson's success at Old Trafford Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can replicate Sir Alex Ferguson’s success as he pays tribute to his former boss on the 40th anniversary of his appointment; Watch Man Utd vs Aston Villa live on Sky ; kick-off at 4.30pm this Sunday William Bitibiri Football Journalist @williambitibiri Friday 6 November 2026 16:19, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Micheal Carrick says ‘success takes time’ and won’t rule out giving Manchester United the same success as Sir Alex Ferguson Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can reach the heights achieved under Sir Alex Ferguson but is not expecting the same level of patience. Friday marks 40 years since Ferguson was appointed United manager on November 6, 1986. It is an anniversary that comes at a particularly significant moment for the club, with Carrick's position in charge still facing intense scrutiny. United's dramatic 3-2 comeback victory over Roma in midweek offered Carrick some much-needed breathing space after a nine-game winless run, but Sunday's Premier League clash against Aston Villa, live on Sky, represents another significant test. messages.text: 'Big shoes to fill' - Sinner parts ways with coach Cahill after five-year run

metadata.summary: Jannik Sinner has parted ways with coach Darren Cahill with Magnus Norman poised to replace the Australian.
metadata.content: Jannik Sinner: Partnership with coach Darren Cahill ends with the Italian winning five Grand Slam titles and achieve No 1 ranking | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Jannik Sinner: Partnership with coach Darren Cahill ends with the Italian winning five Grand Slam titles and achieve No 1 ranking Jannik Sinner has confirmed the end of his hugely successful five-year partnership with coach Darren Cahill with Magnus Norman ‌poised to replace him; You can watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports with the WTA Finals in Indian Wells starting on Sunday Friday 6 November 2026 15:28, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jannik Sinner posted a heartfelt message to Darren Cahill on his social media after parting ways with the coach, following a hugely successful five-year partnership. Vide credit: @janniksin Jannik Sinner has parted ways with coach Darren Cahill with Magnus Norman poised to replace the Australian. Sinner has won five Grand Slam titles and spent 95 weeks as world No 1 under the guidance of the veteran Australian, who worked alongside Italian Simone Vagnozzi, but will team up with Swede Magnus Norman on December 1. Cahill had planned to retire at the end of last season but the pair made a bet that, if Sinner won the Wimbledon title, he could decide on the 61-year-old's future, and he stayed on for another year. messages.text: Russell to take grid penalty at Sao Paulo GP

metadata.summary: George Russell will take a five-place grid penalty at this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix for use of a fresh Mercedes engine.
metadata.content: George Russell: Mercedes driver to take five-place grid penalty at Sao Paulo GP for engine change | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to main content George Russell: Mercedes driver to take five-place grid penalty at Sao Paulo GP for engine change Mercedes driver was always expected to take one more grip drop before the season ended after Malaysia power-unit failure; sixth internal combustion engine of season being fitted; watch Friday's practice sessions from the Sao Paulo GP at 3.30pm and 7pm live on Sky Sports F1 Friday 6 November 2026 14:04, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli having won the world title at the last race, George Russell reflects on what's been a tough season for him. George Russell will take a five-place grid penalty at this weekend's Sao Paulo Grand Prix for use of a fresh Mercedes engine. The Briton was always expected to take an additional grid penalty before the end of the season after the failure that stopped his car at the Bahrain GP in Malaysia, although the track for doing so had not been clear. Russell took a fifth engine of the season, and other power unit parts, at last month's Singapore GP, which dropped him to the back of the field there.
